evidence.measured: R6 Linux ARM64, 3 CPUs/2 GiB, 100 documents: explicit begin/read/commit averaged 0.0193/0.0268/8.1587 ms over 200 transactions, with 200 durable flushes. Autocommit at one client: 234.53 ops/s; 4.956 of 5.006 s inside the forwarding journal Flush wrapper, 1,174 flushes and 89,224 WAL bytes for 1,174 reads. Windows 8-client stack: six workers at GatedJournalLog.AppendCommitAsync monitor entry, one at TransactionManager.BeginAsync monitor entry and one at Storage.AwaitCommitDurable; 207.96 aggregate contention-seconds over 30.03 s. tasks.rootCause: The read-only state is not used to suppress lifecycle WAL. Every successful autocommit read drains 76 bytes of begin/commit frames and normally forces the journal. GetAsync itself does not execute OQL; statement parsing cannot explain this read latency.
